applicable_learner_decisions: Diagnose NSTEMI by integrating an ischemic presentation, regional ECG change, and a dynamic high-sensitivity troponin rise.
shared_features: diaphoresis or autonomic symptoms can occur
a dangerous cause requires prompt exclusion
edges.plausible_error: The learner overweights chest pain and danger while ignoring the territorial ischemic ECG change and dynamic troponin pattern.
edges.neighboring_choice: Pulmonary embolism as the cause of acute chest symptoms.
edges.decisive_discriminant: PE becomes competitive with sudden dyspnea, pleuritic pain, hypoxemia, hemoptysis, VTE risk, or a probability-linked PE work-up; the stem instead supplies a regional ischemic ECG change and dynamic troponin rise without those PE features.
excluded_contexts: Exclude if PE probability features make PE equal or more likely.

applicable_learner_decisions: Diagnose NSTEMI by integrating an ischemic presentation, regional ECG change, and a dynamic high-sensitivity troponin rise.
shared_features: a life-threatening vascular cause is possible
edges.plausible_error: The learner treats any severe chest pain in a hypertensive patient as dissection despite absent high-risk aortic features.
edges.neighboring_choice: Acute aortic syndrome as the cause of chest pain.
edges.decisive_discriminant: Dissection is supported by abrupt maximal-onset chest/back pain, pulse or blood-pressure differences, or malperfusion; the stem explicitly lacks those features and instead has a territorial ischemic pattern.
excluded_contexts: Exclude if abrupt maximal pain, pulse deficit, neurologic deficit, or aortic regurgitation makes AAS genuinely competitive.

applicable_learner_decisions: Diagnose NSTEMI by integrating an ischemic presentation, regional ECG change, and a dynamic high-sensitivity troponin rise.
shared_features: pain may follow a recent viral illness in some cases
edges.plausible_error: The learner sees chest pain plus an ST change and recalls pericarditis without checking pain quality or territorial versus widespread ECG distribution.
edges.neighboring_choice: Acute pericarditis as an inflammatory chest-pain syndrome.
edges.decisive_discriminant: Pericarditis is characteristically sharp, pleuritic, positional, and associated with widespread ST elevation or PR depression; the stem has pressure-like exertional pain and regional ischemic ST depression.
excluded_contexts: Exclude if the pain is pleuritic/positional or the ECG is diffuse rather than territorial.

applicable_learner_decisions: Diagnose NSTEMI by integrating an ischemic presentation, regional ECG change, and a dynamic high-sensitivity troponin rise.
shared_features: symptoms can be described as burning or pressure
edges.plausible_error: The learner anchors on a recent meal or retrosternal burning and prematurely labels reflux.
edges.neighboring_choice: GERD as a noncardiac cause of retrosternal symptoms.
edges.decisive_discriminant: GERD is favoured by heartburn/regurgitation and is established only after adequate cardiac evaluation for unexplained chest pain; regional ischemic ECG change with a dynamic troponin rise cannot be dismissed as reflux.
excluded_contexts: Exclude if the stem lacks objective ischemia or supplies dominant typical reflux features after cardiac causes are addressed.

applicable_learner_decisions: Choose serial ECGs and assay-specific repeat high-sensitivity troponin when early initial ACS tests are nondiagnostic.
shared_features: both pathways can involve biomarkers and urgent imaging
edges.plausible_error: The learner substitutes a generic dangerous-chest-pain work-up for probability-directed PE testing.
edges.neighboring_choice: D-dimer followed by CTPA as a PE diagnostic pathway.
edges.decisive_discriminant: D-dimer/CTPA is probability-driven for suspected PE; absence of dyspnea, pleuritic pain, hypoxemia, VTE risk, or PE-likely assessment leaves serial ECG and hs-cTn as the scenario-bound ACS investigation.
excluded_contexts: Exclude if the case has moderate/high PE probability or a positive probability-linked D-dimer.

applicable_learner_decisions: Choose serial ECGs and assay-specific repeat high-sensitivity troponin when early initial ACS tests are nondiagnostic.
shared_features: initial cardiac tests may be nondiagnostic
edges.plausible_error: The learner equates severity with aortic catastrophe and orders CTA without aortic risk features.
edges.neighboring_choice: Immediate CT angiography of the aorta.
edges.decisive_discriminant: Aortic CTA is indicated when acute aortic syndrome is suspected from abrupt maximal pain or malperfusion features; those are absent, while persistent ischemic suspicion after early nondiagnostic tests calls for serial ECG and hs-cTn.
excluded_contexts: Exclude if the history or examination raises genuine acute aortic syndrome suspicion.

applicable_learner_decisions: Choose serial ECGs and assay-specific repeat high-sensitivity troponin when early initial ACS tests are nondiagnostic.
shared_features: echocardiography can be relevant in both cardiac disorders
edges.plausible_error: The learner orders inflammatory markers and echocardiography after recalling pericarditis from any chest pain.
edges.decisive_discriminant: The case lacks pleuritic/positional pain and widespread ST/PR changes; its early nondiagnostic ACS tests require serial ECG and hs-cTn rather than a pericarditis-first pathway.
excluded_contexts: Exclude if pericarditic pain, diffuse ECG changes, rub, or effusion evidence is present.

applicable_learner_decisions: Choose serial ECGs and assay-specific repeat high-sensitivity troponin when early initial ACS tests are nondiagnostic.
shared_features: normal early cardiac tests can tempt premature closure
edges.plausible_error: The learner interprets one normal early troponin and ECG as adequate exclusion of ACS and pivots to reflux testing.
edges.neighboring_choice: Upper endoscopy or reflux monitoring for GERD.
edges.decisive_discriminant: Objective GERD testing for chest pain follows adequate cardiac evaluation; one early nondiagnostic ECG and hs-cTn do not complete that evaluation when ACS suspicion persists.
excluded_contexts: Exclude if an adequate cardiac evaluation is complete and typical reflux/alarm features make GI testing the active decision.

applicable_learner_decisions: Choose immediate fibrinolysis followed by rapid PCI-centre transfer for an early STEMI when primary PCI cannot occur within 120 minutes.
shared_features: primary PCI is generally preferred when timely
edges.plausible_error: The learner knows primary PCI is preferred but ignores the scenario's first-medical-contact-to-device delay above 120 minutes.
edges.neighboring_choice: Transfer for primary PCI without giving fibrinolysis.
edges.decisive_discriminant: At a non-PCI centre with an expected device time beyond 120 minutes, no contraindication, early presentation, and low bleeding risk, Canadian guidance supports fibrinolysis rather than accepting the excessive untreated delay.
excluded_contexts: Exclude if primary PCI can be achieved within 120 minutes or fibrinolysis is contraindicated.

applicable_learner_decisions: Choose immediate fibrinolysis followed by rapid PCI-centre transfer for an early STEMI when primary PCI cannot occur within 120 minutes.
shared_features: clinical and ECG reperfusion can be assessed locally
rescue PCI is needed after failed lysis
edges.plausible_error: The learner remembers rescue PCI but omits routine pharmacoinvasive transfer after apparently successful lysis.
edges.neighboring_choice: Give fibrinolysis and transfer only if reperfusion fails.
edges.decisive_discriminant: Canadian pharmacoinvasive guidance requires routine rapid PCI-centre transfer after fibrinolysis and angiography within 24 hours even when reperfusion appears successful.
excluded_contexts: Exclude if transfer is genuinely unavailable and the item explicitly tests contingency planning rather than the recommended pathway.

applicable_learner_decisions: Choose immediate fibrinolysis followed by rapid PCI-centre transfer for an early STEMI when primary PCI cannot occur within 120 minutes.
shared_features: cardiac troponin is central to myocardial infarction classification
serial testing is appropriate for nondiagnostic suspected ACS
chest pain can have nonischemic causes
edges.plausible_error: The learner overgeneralizes the serial-troponin rule from uncertain NSTE-ACS to an ECG-diagnostic STEMI.
edges.neighboring_choice: Wait for serial high-sensitivity troponin before selecting reperfusion.
edges.decisive_discriminant: The stem establishes diagnostic STEMI; current ACS guidance states that reperfusion must not be delayed pending biomarkers.
excluded_contexts: Exclude if the ECG is nondiagnostic and the case truly requires serial testing before classification.

applicable_learner_decisions: Choose immediate fibrinolysis followed by rapid PCI-centre transfer for an early STEMI when primary PCI cannot occur within 120 minutes.
edges.plausible_error: The learner responds to severe pain and hypertension with an aortic pathway despite absent acute-aortic discriminants and a diagnostic territorial STEMI.
edges.neighboring_choice: Begin anti-impulse therapy and obtain urgent aortic CTA.
edges.decisive_discriminant: Aortic anti-impulse therapy and CTA require suspected acute aortic syndrome; the case lacks abrupt maximal-onset pain, pulse/BP asymmetry, and malperfusion and instead has diagnostic STEMI requiring immediate reperfusion.
excluded_contexts: Exclude if high-risk aortic features make dissection a genuine competing emergency.
